instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Acknowledge Our History
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you box our allotment photo, label that summer properly. It wasn't three months wasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three carrots is the yield. We got up every morning to water them together. Don't reduce the whole record to the harvest figure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please do. When someone asks about it, start with those mornings. Give them the full account before you get to the three carrots.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't bin our ferry ticket yet. Put it with the overtime slips; that weekend took three late shifts each.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the ferry. I hate being reminded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: File it as a missed crossing, not a wasted weekend. We stayed together anyway. Keep the hotel receipt with it, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the receipt, then. That part was lovely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write that on the envelope: 'That part was lovely.' In your handwriting, please. I can supply the dates; I need those words from you.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Choose the Relationship
cards.instruction: Make someone prioritize this connection over a competing person, promise, or opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let work ring. We finish reading a vow before approving it; please look at the sentence we're choosing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The client won't sign unless I'm there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give this commitment ten uninterrupted minutes first. Start at 'I promise,' not the middle. I need you here for the words we're keeping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask Maya to cover. She'll want a reason.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her we're choosing our wedding vows. Put that in the calendar as an appointment, please, not a blank space someone can book over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay for dinner with me. I've learned your mother's dumplings, and they're ready to steam. We serve them now, not between other appointments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director's at the networking dinner. I could get promoted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decline before we start the steamer. Eight minutes, lid closed; I won't have you taking calls halfway through the meal I've made for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Freeze them. We'll have them tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We froze our anniversary dinner on that promise. Fill the steamer to this line, please, and tell the director you're already having dinner with me.

cards.title: Remember Me Correctly
cards.instruction: Create small tests of whether someone remembers your preferences, stories, or shared history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take the tea through, identify my cup, please. We serve people what they actually use.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you just take one? Everyone's waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've had breakfast together for twelve years. This shouldn't require a conference. Which cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The blue one. Your name's underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correct. Turn it upright, please. Now, how much milk? Answer before you look for another label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you caption our missed-boat photo, repeat what I said on the quay. A caption should be accurate, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember you laughing. Not the words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Laughter isn't a quotation. I'll give you the beginning: 'That's the last time we trust...' Complete it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just write 'Happy memories'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the answer. Was it your watch, my French, or the man selling watches? Choose one, please; we aren't short of evidence.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Let Go of the Grudge
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender resentment, distance, or a claim that keeps the relationship stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come sit beside me for dinner. I missed your opening night; let's not arrange another empty seat to correct the first one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left that seat empty. You can have one tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I got last night wrong. Tonight I need you here, not represented by a plate. Move it over, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm still going to tell you what you missed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please do. Start with the first scene; I'll listen without interrupting. Beside me, please, so you don't have to deliver it across the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me carry a box. Missing your birthday doesn't make me incompetent with your glassware; I'll pack it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I needed you then. You didn't show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Let me get one thing right today. Give me something fragile; I'll support the base, not drag it by the tape.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The birthday glasses. Still wrapped, since nobody came.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry them upright. At the new place, will you let me unwrap two? I'd like to use one with you.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Pulled Away First
cards.instruction: Hide your role in creating the distance while working urgently to repair it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your taxi comes, let's restart our letters. I've brought paper and stamps; we'll get the correspondence running properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You never answered my last three.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Postal delays. We'll remove that variable: write the first letters here and exchange them before you leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I handed you the last one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit here while I write your reply. I'll hand it to you before the taxi comes; you can check every line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's your new key. Test it in the front door, then the kitchen door, please. I've made your favourite lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the lock without telling me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This key works in both. Turn it fully before you push; we'll check the access before the food gets cold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stood outside on my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then come through the kitchen door now. I'll put candles by your plate. Wait until they're lit, please; we're doing the birthday lunch properly.
